Subject: Production outage in us-west-2 — 90% throughput drop and 5xx spike

Soojin —

We're seeing a severe drop in throughput for our production traffic routed to us-west-2. Over the last 12 minutes we measured ~90% drop in successful requests and a sustained 5xx rate hovering 28%. This is impacting customer checkout flows; we've already escalated internally and customers are spinning up support calls.

Key datapoints attached (veridian-error-sample-logs.txt and a 5-minute KPI snapshot). Can Redwood perform a cross-region failover to us-west-1 immediately? If there are tradeoffs (latency increase, partial feature degradation) tell me now so we can inform customers.

We need an exec-level bridge if there's any gating — please advise next steps and estimated ETA.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Head of Platform, Veridian.ai

Subject: Re: Production outage in us-west-2 — 90% throughput drop and 5xx spike

Alyssa — thanks for the data and flag. We're on it.

Short answer: we can enact an emergency regional redirect from us-west-2 -> us-west-1 within ~12-18 minutes, expecting ~10–18% additional median latency for affected routes. There is a small risk (feature flags tied to AZ-local caches) that some in-flight KV-cache dependent operations may return transient errors; we will enable cache warm-up and a throttle policy to mitigate.

Proposed immediate actions (please confirm):
- Authorize cross-region redirect and temporary prioritization of Veridian's traffic (we'll create a targeted routing rule).
- Open an exec bridge (we'll start a bridge and invite Redwood SI/infra + Veridian ops).
- Agree on fallback: if error rate does not drop within 10 minutes post-redirect, we'll pause the redirect and fallback to read-only mode for checkout flows.

I am looping in Connor (serving runtime) and Sean (customer escalation) now. If you authorize, reply "REDIRECT OK" and we'll push.

— Soojin Lee
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production outage in us-west-2 — brief root cause & mitigation plan

Alyssa / Soojin — quick technical note from runtime:

Observed behaviour (preliminary):
- One AZ in us-west-2 has a controller-side queue amplification that saturated KV-cache eviction paths.
- Result: massive tail latency/queueing -> backpressure on GPU pods -> 502/503 responses at the gateway layer.

Immediate mitigations we will execute in parallel:
1) Targeted routing change: divert Veridian production routes off the problematic AZ first, then to us-west-1 if necessary.
2) Enable a temporary token-based throttling policy on heavy non-critical routes to reduce burst load (~20% throttle planned).
3) Warm-up KV caches in us-west-1 using replay of recent prefixes (safe, read-only warm-up) to reduce cold-cache errors post-swap.

Estimated timings: routing change -> 6–12 minutes; cache warm-up -> 8–15 minutes; monitoring stabilization -> 10 minutes post-divert. We'll attach an execution log to the bridge.

Attachments referenced: veridian-error-sample-logs.txt (error traces).

— Connor O'Brien
Director, Serving Runtime

Alyssa — update after execution:

Timeline:
- 08:20 PT: started targeted AZ drain in us-west-2 (divert off AZ-a)
- 08:29 PT: initiated cross-region redirect to us-west-1 for Veridian production routes
- 08:35 PT: KV-cache warm-up complete in us-west-1
- 08:41 PT: observed sustained drop in 5xx rate from 28% -> 2.3% and throughput restored to ~94% of baseline (graph: kpi-5min-graph.png)

Current status: traffic stabilized, majority of routes healthy. We have a short-lived spike in tail latency (+14% median for affected endpoints) while caches warm; no further 5xx bursts observed in the last 15 minutes.

Immediate next steps:
- We'll keep the routing redirect in place for 6 hours while we monitor; gradual re-introduction to us-west-2 will start when health metrics show sustained stability for 30 minutes.
- Post-mortem: Connor will own an RCA and propose a permanent routing policy to avoid AZ-local saturation. ETA for RCA: 72 hours.
- Commercial: Sean, please advise on credit / SLA remediation path; I recommend an offer of 10% service credit for the incident window given customer impact.

Bridge link: https://redwood.app/bridges/2026-08-19-VER-bridge (opened at 08:10 PT).

If anything regresses immediately ping the bridge and we'll act.

— Soojin Lee
